description: Raw sf_evidence and sf_heinlein responses captured by the WI-SF-0113 canary (gpt-oss:20b through Ollama). Only the response fields are kept; run ids, absolute paths and usage fields are dropped.

evidence.paraphrase: Explanation attributing bell sound to an owl's behavior.
evidence.quote: the sound proceeded from a very large owl, in a hollow tree; a sort of learned owl, that continually knocked its head against the branches.

evidence.paraphrase: People express curiosity and plan investigation.
evidence.quote: A long time passed, and people said to each other— 'I wonder if there is a church out in the wood? The bell has a tone that is wondrous sweet; let us stroll thither, and examine the matter nearer.'

evidence.paraphrase: King's promise creates future reward for discovering source.
evidence.quote: The king of the country was also observant of it, and vowed that he who could discover whence the sounds proceeded, should have the title of 'Universal Bell-ringer,' even if it were not really a bell.

evidence.paraphrase: Children express desire to pursue bell.
evidence.quote: They all immediately felt a wish to go thither; all except three.

evidence.paraphrase: Characters confront discrepancy between expectation and reality.
evidence.quote: Now we are there! In reality the bell does not exist; it is only a fancy that people have taken into their heads!

evidence.paraphrase: Description of the absence of various social problems in the world.
evidence.quote: There were no prisons, no slums, no insane asylums, no cripples, no poverty, no wars.

evidence.paraphrase: Explanation that disease and aging have been eliminated.
evidence.quote: All diseases were conquered. So was old age.

evidence.paraphrase: Indication of a cure for aging allowing people to live 200 years.
evidence.quote: A sardonic old man, about two hundred years old, sat on a stepladder, painting a mural he did not like.

evidence.paraphrase: Extrapolation of the consequences of no population control.
evidence.quote: Without population control, human beings would now be packed on this surface of this old planet like drupelets on a blackberry! Think of it!

evidence.paraphrase: Violent act resulting in death, constituting a catastrophe.
evidence.quote: Wehling shot Dr. Hitz dead. 'There's room for one--a great big one,' he said.

evidence.paraphrase: Reaction of Wehling to the situation in the waiting room.
evidence.quote: Wehling, the waiting father, mumbled something without raising his head. And then he fell silent again.

evidence.paraphrase: Painter's reaction after witnessing the killings.
evidence.quote: The painter sat on the top of his stepladder, looking down reflectively on the sorry scene.

evidence.paraphrase: Idealistic opening statement contrasting later violence.
evidence.quote: Everything was perfectly swell.

evidence.paraphrase: Children’s desire to seek the bell.
evidence.quote: They all immediately felt a wish to go thither; all except three.

evidence.paraphrase: Contrasting belief vs reality about bell.
evidence.quote: Now we are there! In reality the bell does not exist; it is only a fancy that people have taken into their heads!

evidence.paraphrase: Introduction of bell sound into world.
evidence.quote: People said 'The Evening Bell is sounding, the sun is setting.'

evidence.paraphrase: Sunset marking passage of time.
evidence.quote: The sun now set: the atmosphere glowed like fire.

heinlein_criteria.rationale: Story explicitly states the bell does not exist, indicating a new condition (phantom bell) different from reality.
The phantom bell drives the plot; characters seek it, making it essential to story.
Plot centers on human children and adults reacting to bell; problem is human.
Human desire to find bell arises from phantom bell phenomenon.
Phantom bell can be explained by auditory hallucination or environmental acoustic effect; no established facts violated.
